sanskrit: jīmūtasyeva bhavati pratīkaṃ yad varmī yāti samadām upasthe | anāviddhayā tanvā jaya tvaṃ sa tvā varmaṇo mahimā pipartu ||
english: His countenance becomes like that of a thunder-cloud when, clad in armour, he goes into the lap of battle. With body unpierced, conquer thou; may the greatness of the armour carry thee through.

sanskrit: dhanvanā gā dhanvanājiṃ jayema dhanvanā tīvrāḥ samado jayema | dhanuḥ śatror apakāmaṃ kṛṇotu dhanvanā sarvāḥ pṛtanā jayema ||
english: With the bow let us win cattle; with the bow let us win contests; with the bow let us win fierce battles. May the bow turn the enemy's desire away; with the bow let us conquer all armies.

sanskrit: vakṣyantīved ā ganīganti karṇaṃ priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ pariṣasvajānā | yoṣeva śiṅkte vitatādhi dhanvañ jyā iyaṃ samiti pārayantī ||
english: Hissing repeatedly, she draws close to the ear, embracing her dear friend. Like a woman she whispers to him stretched upon the bow — this bowstring carries him safe through the assembly of battle.

sanskrit: te ācarantī samaneva yoṣā māteva putraṃ pipṛtām upasthe | apa śatrūn vidhyatāṃ saṃvidāne ārtnī ime visphurantī amitrān ||
english: Moving together like a woman at the assembly, may she nourish him in her lap as a mother nourishes her son. These two bowstrings, quivering and in accord, shall pierce the foes and repel the enemies.

sanskrit: bahvīnāṃ pitā bahur asya putro vyacaḥ kṛṇoti samado 'vagatya | iṣudhiḥ saṅkāḥ pṛtanāś ca sarvāḥ pṛṣṭhe ninaddho jayati prasūtaḥ ||
english: The father of many, his offspring are many; descending into battle he creates wide space. The quiver, its fastenings, and all the armies — bound upon the back, he conquers when sped forth.

sanskrit: rathe tiṣṭhan nayati vājinaḥ puro yatrayatra kāmayate suṣārathiḥ | abhīśūnāṃ mahimānaṃ panāyata manaḥ paścād anu yacchanti raśmayaḥ ||
english: Standing in the chariot, the skilled charioteer drives the horses forward wherever he desires. Marvel at the greatness of the reins; the reins hold the mind in check from behind.

sanskrit: tīvrān ghoṣān kṛṇvatāṃ vṛṣapāṇayo 'śvā rathebhiḥ saha vājayantaḥ | apakrāmantaḥ prapadair amitrān kṣiṇanti śatrūṃr anapavyayantaḥ ||
english: Making fierce clamour, the bull-handed warriors, spurring on the horses together with the chariots, destroy the enemies by advancing upon them with their forelegs, crushing the foes without wavering.

sanskrit: rathavāhanaṃ havir asya nāma yatrāyudhaṃ nihitam asya varma | tatrā ratham upa śagmaṃ sadema viśvāhā vayaṃ sumanasyamānāḥ ||
english: "Chariot-bearer" is his oblation-name — there where his weapon is laid and his armour rests. Upon that prosperous chariot may we be seated, all our days gladdening our hearts.

sanskrit: svāduṣaṃsadaḥ pitaro vayodhāḥ kṛcchreśritaḥ śaktīvanto gabhīrāḥ | citrasenā iṣubalā amṛdhrāḥ satovīrā uravo vrātasāhāḥ ||
english: Sweet in assembly are our forefathers, bestowers of vigour, taking refuge in difficulty, mighty and profound; of brilliant host, strong in arrows, irresistible, heroic in battle, broad-ranged, overcoming hordes.

sanskrit: brahmaṇāsaḥ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ śive no dyāvāpṛthivī anehasā | pūṣā naḥ pātu dūritād ṛtāvṛdho rakṣā mākir ṇo aghaśaṃsa īśata ||
english: Brahman-knowing forefathers, partakers of Soma — may Heaven and Earth be auspicious and free of distress for us. May Pūṣan, increaser of cosmic order, guard us from evil-going; protect us — let no evil-voiced one have power over us.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir naḥ pari pātu paścād utottarasmād adharād aghāyoḥ | indraḥ purastād uta madhyato naḥ sakhā sakhibhyo varivaḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: May Bṛhaspati guard us from behind and from above, from below, from the one who would do us harm. May Indra guard us from the front and from the midst; may he, the friend, make wide space for his friends.

sanskrit: suparṇaṃ vaste mṛgo asyā danto gobhiḥ saṃnaddhā patati prasūtā | yatrā naraḥ saṃ ca vi ca dravanti tad asmabhyam iṣavaḥ śarma yacchān ||
english: The eagle's feather she wears; her tooth is the fawn; bound with cowhide sinew she flies forth when sped. Where men surge together and scatter — there may these arrows grant us shelter.

sanskrit: suparṇo vāso yad u sarpir āsā mano hiraṇyam iṣavaḥ patatrī | māsmāṅ arann amuta āpatantīr itaḥ prahitāḥ savitar jayantu ||
english: The eagle is her garment; clarified butter her mouth; mind her gold; the arrows are the winged ones. Let them not strike us as they swoop from yonder — sped hence, O Savitṛ, may they conquer.

sanskrit: ahir iva bhogair pary eti bāhuṃ jyāyā hetim apabādhamānaḥ | hastaghno viśvā vayunāni vidvān pumān pumāṃsaṃ pari pātu mṛtyoḥ ||
english: Like a serpent with its coils it winds about the arm, warding off the bowstring's stroke. The hand-guard, knowing all the ways of movement, a man shall guard a man from death.

sanskrit: ā jaṅghanti sānv eṣāṃ jaghanām̐ upa jighnate | aśvājani tra pracodaya- -aśvān samatsu pādaya ||
english: They strike the ridge of their backs; they smite upon their haunches. O horse-whip, urge them on; plant the horses firm in the battles.

sanskrit: divas pṛthivyāḥ pary oja ābhṛtaṃ vanaspatibhyaḥ pari saṃbhṛtaṃ sahaḥ | apām ojmānaṃ pari gobhir ābhṛtam indrasya vajraṃ haviṣā rathaṃ yaja ||
english: Vigour gathered from Heaven and Earth, might assembled from the forest trees, the swelling power of the waters — brought round with cowhides: with oblation worship the chariot as Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: indrasya vajro marutām anīkaṃ mitrasya garbho varuṇasya nābhiḥ | semāṃ no havyadātiṃ juṣāṇo deva ratha prati havyā gṛbhāya ||
english: Thou art Indra's thunderbolt, the battle-face of the Maruts, the womb of Mitra, the navel of Varuṇa. So, O divine chariot, enjoying this our gift of oblation, receive thou the offered portions.

sanskrit: vanaspate vīḍvaṅgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ | gobhiḥ saṃnaddho ratha vīḍayasva- -āsthātā te jayatu jetvāni ||
english: O Forest Lord, be thou of firm limb; be our friend who carries us forward, possessed of good heroes. Bound with cowhides, O chariot, make thyself firm; may he who mounts thee conquer what is to be conquered.

sanskrit: upa śvāsaya pṛthivīm uta dyāṃ purutrā te manutāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat | sa dundubhe sajūr indreṇa devair dūrād davīyo apa sedha śatrūn ||
english: Cause Earth and Heaven to resound; let the wide-spread world take note of thee, in many places. O war-drum, in unison with Indra and the gods, drive the enemies away — ever farther away.

sanskrit: ā krandaya balam ojo na ā dhā abhi ṣṭana duritā bādhamānaḥ | apa sedha dundubhe ducchunām ita indrasya muṣṭir asi vīḍayasva ||
english: Roar aloud; lay power and might into us; thunder forth, pressing back misfortunes. Drive away ill-omen, O war-drum, from hence; thou art the fist of Indra — make thyself strong.

sanskrit: prāmūñ jayābhīme jayantu ketumad dundubhir vāvadītu | sam aśvaparṇāḥ patayantu no naro 'smākam indra rathino jayantu ||
english: May they conquer going forward; may they conquer here in this fearful fray; may the banner-bearing war-drum resound aloud. May our horse-winged men take flight together; O Indra, may our chariot-warriors conquer.

sanskrit: indro rathāya prapadaṃ kṛṇotu yam adhyaṣṭhān maghavā jayantām | irya iva paśubhir yuyotu gopā ariṣṭo jātaḥ prathamaḥ siṣāsan ||
english: May Indra prepare the footing for the chariot; may those whom Maghavan has mounted be victorious. Like a cowherd he yokes together with cattle; born unhurt, the foremost, he who would conquer.

sanskrit: parjanyasyeva stanayitnur āsor indrāgnyor iva cekhidyate ghoṣo asya | sāhasro vīraḥ śataṃ sasanvān ayutaṃ sasanvān ratha mṛḍeha ||
english: Like the thunder of Parjanya is the roar of its breath; like that of Indra and Agni its clamour rings out. A warrior of a thousand, winning a hundred, winning ten thousand — O chariot, be gracious here.

sanskrit: śyenasya pakṣau hariṇasya bāhū indrasya muṣṭir marutām anīkam | gobhiḥ saṃnaddho asi vīḍayasva ||
english: The wings of an eagle, the arms of a deer, the fist of Indra, the battle-face of the Maruts — bound with cowhides thou art; make thyself firm.

sanskrit: ud yaṃyamīti sahiteva bāhū ubhe sicau yajate bhīma ṛñjan | uc chukram atkam ajate śacībhir navā mātṛbhyo vasanā jahāti ||
english: He lifts his arms together, stretching them as one; both his flanks he adorns, fearsome in his gleaming. He drives forth the bright mantle with his powers; he casts off the new garments from the mothers.

sanskrit: ugrau te nemī pavī ta ugrā ugrāḥ śaṅkavo bṛhato rathasya | īṣātra veṇavo namatis ta ugrā- -agniś cakṣuḥ pravayaṇaṃ rathasya | tenāmitrān pramṛṇan yāhi śatrūn ||
english: Fierce are thy rims, fierce are thy tires, fierce are the pins of the great chariot. The tongue-shaft and the bamboo reeds, thy bendings are fierce; Agni is the eye, the forward-runner of the chariot. Grinding down the non-allies, go thou against the foes.

sanskrit: arā nābhayo balam it te akṣa ugrau te koṣau saha nisyadābhyām | āṇyor vadhrān uta koṣaghorā sthānaṃ bandha uta vandhuraṃ te ||
english: The spokes and the hubs — that is thy strength, O axle; fierce are thy two boxes together with those who sit in them. The leather thongs of the pins, the box-sheaths, the standing place, the fastening, and thy seat — all are firm.

sanskrit: goṣṭhe balaṃ mṛga ekam aṅgaṃ parā kramadhvaṃ maha ā suvanta | abhīśavo hatānena vṛtram ayaṃ kṣatreṇa prajayāstūgraḥ ||
english: Strength is the stall; one limb is the fawn — stride forth; press on into the great realm. The reins have slain Vṛtra with this one; fierce is he with lordship and progeny.

sanskrit: ā tiṣṭha jiṣṇus tarasā sapatnān sāhasro vīraḥ pramṛṇan yāhi śatrūn | pṛṣṭiyuge kṛṇutaṃ vīryāṇi tad etām etaṃ ratham asya śagme ||
english: Mount, O conquering one; with swiftness overcome the rivals; a warrior of a thousand, grinding down, go against the foes. Perform heroic deeds in the span of the back-ridge — thus: welcome this very chariot of his.

sanskrit: aṣṭau cakṣūṃṣi kavayaḥ saṃ namantv aśvā prākāśā ṛju dhāvayantaḥ | anu tvā skambho dadatāṃ piteva cakramāṇam ainaṃ dhatsvopasthe pra tirāty āyuḥ ||
english: May the eight eyes of the seers bow in unison; may the illumined horses run straight. May the pillar-post support thee like a father — as it revolves, hold him in thy lap; may his life-span be extended.

sanskrit: kavibhiḥ syūtaḥ sa rathe vibaddhaḥ sa dhanvadhir dhanucitte jajāna | anuprāsyemāni pṛthumadhyamāny aśvebhyaḥ śaṃtvāya kavibhiḥ kṛtāni tebhiṣ ṭe śarma yacchantu devāḥ ||
english: Sewn by the seers, he is fastened in the chariot; born in the mind of the bow, keeper of the bow. These broad-middled ones, fashioned by the seers, are to be cast before the horses for their welfare — may the gods grant thee shelter through them.
